e: The keys must be managed outside AWS, so encrypt the data client-side in the company's data center (using its own keys) before uploading it over HTTPS to S3, which covers encryption in transit and at rest. SSE-S3 and SSE-KMS keys are managed in AWS.

API Gateway with Lambda handles the notification intake and basic validation without servers, and the long-running backend runs on ECS with Fargate, where compute and memory are configurable per task and no infrastructure is managed. EKS with self-managed nodes, EKS Anywhere, or EC2 Spot require managing infrastructure.

Amazon Cognito user pools scale to millions of users and offer adaptive (risk-based) authentication that requires MFA when sign-ins come from unusual locations, IP addresses, or devices. Identity pools don't authenticate users, and IAM users or IAM Identity Center don't provide risk-based adaptive MFA at that scale.

AWS Glue (serverless ETL) transforms the S3 data daily and loads it into Redshift Serverless, which is an MPP data warehouse, and Redshift ML lets analysts create and train ML models with SQL. EMR isn't serverless, Aurora isn't MPP, and Athena isn't a data warehouse.

AWS Outposts racks run AWS services (including EKS) in the company's own data center, keeping data local for compliance while using managed AWS services. Local Zones are in AWS facilities, and Snowmobile or Snowball Edge don't run EKS as a managed data center service.

An S3 File Gateway exposes NFS file shares backed by S3, so the workloads keep using NFS while the data scales in S3, and lifecycle policies move data to cheaper classes. EFS storage costs more than S3, and volume gateways provide block volumes rather than NFS.

The functions are CPU intensive and already high concurrency, so more memory (which also adds CPU) shortens run time and can reduce cost per message when set per Compute Optimizer recommendations, and reserved concurrency avoids the extra charge of provisioned concurrency. Decreasing memory slows CPU-bound work and raises latency.

Storing images in ECR (which ECS pulls from natively) with scan on push scans every new image for CVEs with no workload changes. Macie and S3-based approaches don't scan container images, and moving to EKS is a larger change.

An EventBridge rule matching AWS Batch job SUCCEEDED events can target an EventBridge API destination that calls the third-party HTTP API with basic (username and password) authentication, entirely serverless with no code. The other options add Lambda or API Gateway components.

The vendor places an NLB in front of the RDS database and exposes it with AWS PrivateLink (an endpoint service), and the company creates an interface endpoint in its VPC, giving private connectivity across accounts without internet, Direct Connect, or VPN. VPC peering alone doesn't solve it for the stated constraints.

Putting the Managed Grafana workspace in the VPC and using the RDS database's private endpoint keeps the data off the public internet. Public endpoints expose the database, and PrivateLink from a non-VPC workspace isn't how Managed Grafana connects to RDS.

AWS Glue DataBrew is a no-code visual data preparation tool with prebuilt transformations, data profiling, and data lineage, and recipes can be shared across the company. Glue Studio jobs, EMR Serverless, and Athena SQL require code or don't provide profiling and lineage the same way.

A Route 53 alias or A record for the development hostname pointing to the ALB, with an ALB listener rule (host-based) forwarding that hostname to the target group holding the development instance, keeps working automatically when the instance is replaced. Public IPs would change, and redirects to IPs don't survive replacement.

Amazon MQ is a managed broker that supports AMQP, so the application's messaging code keeps working, and EKS runs the existing Kubernetes containers with little refactoring. SQS doesn't speak AMQP, and EC2 or Lambda require more changes or management.

AWS Global Accelerator with a standard accelerator and the existing NLBs as endpoints routes players over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy Region, reducing end-to-end load time with no architecture changes. ALBs don't fit, equal-weighted DNS doesn't consider latency, and more Regions add cost.

AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP endpoint that writes directly to S3, so legacy vendors keep using SFTP with the least operational overhead. DMS isn't for file transfer, EC2 SFTP servers need maintenance, and S3 File Gateway uses SMB or NFS.

Amazon Comprehend analyzes text for entities, key phrases, and sentiment, so feeding it the Textract output and saving results to S3 gives content and sentiment insights with little overhead. SageMaker requires building a model, and Athena or QuickSight don't perform sentiment analysis.

Kinesis Data Streams ingests the real-time third-party data, and Kinesis Data Firehose delivers the raw data to the S3 bucket, all managed and scalable. DMS and DataSync aren't for streaming ingestion, and Direct Connect isn't an ingestion service.

DynamoDB items are limited to 400 KB, so store the large data as objects in S3 and keep an item with a pointer (the S3 URL) in DynamoDB, which scales to any size with little operational effort. Splitting items, compressing, or DocumentDB add complexity.

Containerize the cron jobs and use EventBridge Scheduler (recurring and one-time schedules, covering a future event) to run them as Fargate tasks, which have no 15-minute limit and need minimal refactoring for 1 to 20 minute jobs. Lambda can't run jobs approaching 20 minutes reliably, and Batch or Step Functions Wait add overhead.

Amazon AppFlow has a native Salesforce connector that loads existing data and ongoing changes to Redshift, and it can use AWS PrivateLink so the data doesn't traverse the public internet, with no development. DataBrew isn't an ingestion connector, and VPN, Direct Connect, or peering to Salesforce aren't available.

Moving the files to S3 with Intelligent-Tiering (using the S3 API from the application) is cheaper than EFS, FSx, or Glacier Flexible Retrieval for files that may still be accessed, optimizing cost with moderate application changes. FSx options cost more, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval isn't suited to an indexed active file store.

An Application Load Balancer supports HTTPS with ACM certificates and advanced request routing, including routing by query string conditions to different target groups. NLBs operate at layer 4 and can't route by query parameters, and Gateway Load Balancers are for appliances.

An Auto Scaling group behind an ALB makes the application tier highly available and scalable, and Aurora Serverless (MySQL-compatible) scales the database automatically and is highly available. Redshift isn't MySQL, a fixed RDS cluster doesn't autoscale, and ElastiCache isn't a MySQL database.

A KMS customer managed key with automatic key rotation (yearly) as the bucket's default SSE-KMS key meets the requirement with no manual work. SSE-S3 keys can't be controlled on a rotation schedule by the customer, manual rotation adds effort, and imported key material requires manual rotation.
